title: Selector pairs and product retention
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\pi$ be a probability distribution on $\Omega$, let $n$ be a natural number, and let $\theta\in[-1,1]$. Sample $x$ from $\pi^{\otimes n}$, then independently at each coordinate retain $x_i$ with probability $(1+\theta)/2$ and otherwise draw a fresh value from $\pi$. The law of the pair of vectors $(x,y)$ equals the law obtained by sampling two independent vectors from $\pi^{\otimes n}$ and applying, coordinatewise, a correlated pair of signs with uniform first sign and second sign agreeing with it with probability $(1+\theta)/2$ to select between the two values.
